definitions.gloss: to accomplish; to carry through; to complete
definitions.explanation: To see a task or challenge through to completion, especially one that was difficult. Emphasizes perseverance and finishing what was started.

examples.japanese: {最後|さいご}までやり{遂|と}げた。
examples.english: I saw it through to the end.

examples.japanese: {難|むずか}しい{仕事|しごと}をやり{遂|と}げる{自信|じしん}がある。
examples.english: I have confidence that I can carry out this difficult job.

examples.japanese: どんなに{辛|つら}くても{途中|とちゅう}で{諦|あきら}めずにやり{遂|と}げることが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: No matter how hard it gets, it's important not to give up halfway and to see it through.

notes:
FORMATION:
A compound verb from やる (to do) + {遂|と}げる (to accomplish). The combination emphasizes completing a task despite difficulty.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {最後|さいご}までやり{遂|と}げる (to see through to the end)
- {仕事|しごと}をやり{遂|と}げる (to complete a job)
- {目標|もくひょう}をやり{遂|と}げる (to achieve a goal)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {成|な}し{遂|と}げる: to accomplish — more formal, used for significant achievements
- やりきる: to do completely — emphasizes exhausting effort
